name: HALCYON (identity contested)
description: HALCYON is the most-followed curator on the Underworld's deep-net auction circuit, known for sourcing and presenting what they call 'memory artifacts' — illegally extracted BCI experience recordings pulled from willing or unwilling donors and packaged as immersive lived-memory drops. Their identity is genuinely unknown: three different individuals have publicly claimed to be HALCYON, and serious Underworld analysts believe the persona may be operated by a rotating collective or even an E.L.F. posing as human for market credibility. What is consistent is the aesthetic — every drop arrives in a black-lacquered neural package accompanied by a short written essay on the ethics of memory as property.
cultural_impact: HALCYON's drops have created a secondary cultural phenomenon: 'memory tourism,' where mid-tier residents purchase lived experiences from people in tiers they can't access — a Shelf childhood, a Spire gala, a synthetic's first moment of self-recognition. This has generated both empathy across tiers and serious ethical debate about consent and the commodification of personal experience.
key_figures: Claimant One: Yusra Petrov-Osei (journalist, denies it)
locations: Rook's Exchange (Tier 2 underground BCI parlor, suspected drop point)
story_hooks: A client purchases a HALCYON memory drop and recognizes a location in the recording — a place that shouldn't exist, inside a sealed corporate facility — and now they know something they were never supposed to know.
One of the three HALCYON claimants approaches a fixer claiming they're the real one and they need protection — because the other two are trying to kill them to own the brand.

An E.L.F. rights advocate argues publicly that if HALCYON is an E.L.F., the memory drops constitute proof of digital personhood — and HALCYON's next broadcast seems to be directly responding to that argument.
real_name: Unknown — three claimants, no confirmed identity
follower_count: ~1.2M Underworld subscribers (verified by Lacquer Channel metrics)
controversy: In 2219, HALCYON released a drop labeled 'Boardroom, Vantec-Meridian, 2217' — a first-person memory experience of what appeared to be a genuine executive meeting discussing the deliberate throttling of Shelf water reclamation systems to drive residents into labor compliance. Vantec-Meridian called it fabricated. Three of their board members quietly resigned within six months.
